The Phoenix Blades were a high elven organization that gained fame for the elimination of enemy commanders before battle. To reward their service and mark their station, their leader was gifted the Infinity Blades. The Phoenix Blades were disbanded when they betrayed a king of the Sunstriders, and are reviled as traitors and assassins in modern Quel'Thalas. Their leader's blades were taken by, and later recovered from, Kael'thas Sunstrider.

Pillarstone Spire is an elevator to the Skolzgal Mill on the surface of the Isle of Dorn in central Ringing Deeps. Mindi Maxlof has gotten herself stranded here and is looking for some assistance with her leafletting. The area is bordered by the Waterworks to the west, Brunwin's Terrace to the north, Shadowvein Extraction Site to the northeast, the Rumbling Wastes to the east, and the Cataract River to the south and southwest. The Cataract River Cruise skyriding race is immediately to the south at overlooking the river.

Pirate Foods and Superstitions is part of the third chapter of the Guest Relations storyline, first made available on 13 November. Pitz Lowe is a goblin located in the Vatworks in Undermine. Among the goblins of the area, he has a good reputation, a fact unknown by his father, an inventor, who hoped he would become one as well. They worked together on machines like G.O.L.E.M., but the old man was often frustrated with Pitz. When an adventurer came in to their workshop, the old man asked them to take G.O.L.E.M. and Pitz for a test run. While out in the streets, Pitz wanted to help out the community by disposing of garbage from the streets. .]] The Ping System allows players to communicate quickly and effectively without relying on voice or text chat. By using the ping wheel, players can highlight locations, objects, or NPCs and convey their intentions to teammates. The system includes five types of pings: Standard, Attack, Warning, On My Way, and Help/Assist, each represented by distinct icons and colors. These pings appear on the screen, mini-map, and optionally in chat, providing clear visual cues for group coordination.
